scheme_name: Scheme for Giving Awards to Senior Artists in Contemporary Art Field
description:
The Scheme for Giving Awards to Senior Artists in the Contemporary Art Field was launched by the Government of India in the year 2006. 

This scheme is administered by the Ministry of Culture. 

The primary objective of this scheme is to recognize and honor the contributions of senior artists who have made significant achievements in the field of contemporary art. 

The scheme aims to promote the arts and encourage the continued creativity of senior artists. 

The awards are intended to provide financial assistance and recognition to artists who have dedicated their lives to the field of contemporary art. 

The awards are given annually. 

The scheme is designed to honor artists who are at least 60 years of age. 

Eligible artists must have a proven track record of work in contemporary art for a minimum of 25 years. 

The awards are conferred based on the merit of the artist's work and their contribution to the field. 

The financial benefit provided under this scheme is a one-time award amount of INR 1,00,000. 

In addition to the monetary award, recipients receive a citation and a trophy. 

The awards are presented during a formal ceremony organized by the Ministry of Culture. 

The ceremony typically takes place in the month of December each year. 

The selection process for the awards involves a committee of experts in the field of contemporary art. 

This committee evaluates the applications based on the quality and impact of the artist's work. 

The committee also considers the artist's contribution to the promotion of contemporary art in India. 

Artists can be nominated for the award by various organizations, including art galleries, cultural institutions, and fellow artists. 

Self-nominations are also accepted under this scheme. 

To apply for the award, the following documents are required: a detailed curriculum vitae, a portfolio of the artist's work, and letters of recommendation from recognized individuals in the field of art. 

The application form can be obtained from the official website of the Ministry of Culture. 

Applications must be submitted by the end of September each year to be considered for that year's awards. 

The Ministry of Culture reviews all applications and announces the awardees by the end of November. 

The awards are aimed at artists working in various mediums, including painting, sculpture, installation, and mixed media. 

The scheme also seeks to encourage inter-generational dialogue in the arts by highlighting the work of senior artists. 

It aims to create a platform for these artists to share their experiences and knowledge with younger generations. 

The awards serve not only as recognition but also as a means to inspire upcoming artists in the contemporary art scene. 

The scheme has seen participation from artists across the country, showcasing the diversity of contemporary art in India. 

The Ministry of Culture has reported that over 100 artists have been honored since the inception of the scheme in 2006. 

The awards have contributed to raising awareness about the importance of preserving and promoting contemporary art in India. 

The scheme also aligns with the broader goals of the Government of India to promote cultural heritage and artistic expression. 

The Ministry of Culture encourages public participation in the arts through various initiatives, including this award scheme. 

The awards are part of a larger set of initiatives aimed at supporting artists and promoting cultural activities in the country. 

The Ministry of Culture can be contacted for more information regarding the scheme at their official office located in New Delhi. 

The contact number for inquiries is +91-11-2338-2000. 

The official website of the Ministry of Culture provides additional details and updates about the scheme. 

The scheme has been positively received by the art community and has garnered support from various stakeholders in the cultural sector. 

The recognition provided through this scheme has helped many artists gain visibility and opportunities for further exhibitions and projects. 

The awards not only acknowledge individual talent but also contribute to the overall growth of the contemporary art ecosystem in India. 

The scheme has been instrumental in fostering a sense of community among senior artists. 

It provides a platform for networking and collaboration among artists from different regions and backgrounds. 

The awards have also led to increased media coverage of contemporary art in India. 

This has helped in elevating the status of contemporary artists in the public eye. 

The Ministry of Culture actively promotes the achievements of awardees through various channels. 

This includes social media campaigns and features in cultural publications. 

The scheme has also inspired similar initiatives in various states across India. 

State governments have launched their own awards to recognize local artists, inspired by the central government's initiative. 

Overall, the Scheme for Giving Awards to Senior Artists in the Contemporary Art Field plays a crucial role in supporting and promoting the arts in India. 

It highlights the importance of recognizing the contributions of senior artists who have shaped the contemporary art landscape. 

The scheme not only provides financial support but also fosters a culture of appreciation for the arts. 

The awards serve as a reminder of the rich artistic heritage of India and the ongoing relevance of contemporary art. 

Through this initiative, the Government of India continues to invest in the cultural fabric of the nation. 

The scheme reflects the government's commitment to nurturing talent and promoting artistic expression across all age groups. 

It stands as a testament to the value placed on creativity and the arts in Indian society. 

The ongoing success of the scheme indicates a positive trend in the recognition of artists and their contributions to culture. 

The awards are a celebration of the enduring legacy of senior artists in contemporary art. 

They inspire future generations to pursue their artistic passions and contribute to the vibrant cultural landscape of India.
